title: Recent intermarriage and endogamy — global updates
note: Compiled from national statistical offices, DHS/NFHS, and peer-reviewed census analyses published roughly 2017–2026. Definitions differ (race, ethnicity, religion, nationality, kin). Prefer each source’s own wording over cross-country ranking.

unitedStates.title: United States — married-couple stock (ACS 2022)
unitedStates.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2022 (Hernandez & Hemez / Census analysis of same-sex and opposite-sex couples).
unitedStates.note: Stock of currently married couples, not newlyweds. Pew’s 2015 newlywed rates (17% overall) remain the best published by-group flow estimates; 2020 ACS race coding changes create a break in microdata trends.

india.title: India — caste, ethnicity, and religion
india.source: Dongardive & Nagdeve (2023), Population Geography, NFHS-5 2019–21; Pew Research Center Religion in India (2019–20 survey); marriage-cohort estimates from NFHS analyses.
india.note: Inter-caste is far more common than interfaith. Pew’s survey finds 99% of married Indians report a same-religion spouse (attitudinal/survey self-report). NFHS-5 couple file yields ~3% inter-religious.

china.title: China — ethnic intermarriage
china.source: Seventh National Population Census analyses (minority interethnic rate 2020); Wang et al. census analysis 1982–2015; Jian (2017) Journal of Chinese Sociology.
china.note: National rates look low because Han are >90% of the population; among ethnic minorities the interethnic rate is much higher and rising. Over 80% of minority interethnic marriages are with Han.

brazil.title: Brazil — interracial unions
brazil.source: PNAD / PNAD Contínua analysis of interracial unions among couples aged 20–24 (Telles tradition; recent update 2002–2022).
brazil.note: Racial categories are White, Brown (parda), Black, and others — more fluid than U.S. race. Interracial union shares have been roughly stable near one-third since the early 2000s after rising through the late 20th century.

japan.title: Japan — international marriages
japan.source: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare vital statistics via IPSS Population Statistics of Japan 2025, Table 6-16.
japan.note: Nationality of spouses, not ethnicity. Peak international share was mid-2000s (~5–6%); COVID years compressed absolute counts; 2023 share of marriages with at least one foreign spouse is about 3.8% (excluding two-foreigner couples from the ‘international with Japanese’ total if preferred — here we report both Japanese nationals vs any foreign involvement).

denmark.title: Denmark — mixed unions among 1.5- and second-generation immigrants
denmark.source: Elwert & Tegunimataka register study (unions formed 1986–2016 among 1.5- and second-generation immigrants from 120 origins).
denmark.note: Share who ever formed a mixed union with a native Dane by age 40 (or censoring). Religion of origin country is the strongest predictor; Turkish, Pakistani and Somali origins remain highly endogamous.

pakistan.title: Pakistan — consanguinity (DHS)
pakistan.source: Pakistan Demographic and Health Survey 2017–18; BMC Women’s Health reanalysis of PDHS waves 1990–2018.
pakistan.note: First-cousin marriage ~50% has been essentially flat for three decades. Broader consanguinity (any relative) is about 64%.
